assessment_scope.source_boundary: Only the subject's single curated item, reviewed-dedicated-analysis: the canonical V2 character reconstruction model MHA_SP2_CHISAKI_OVERHAUL_CHARACTER_RECONSTRUCTION_MODEL.md at basis_commit, read in full as reviewed repository analysis of the Japanese main manga V01-V42 with the source-labeled Ultra Archive, Ultra Analysis and Ultra Age claims its CO-SUP-01 to CO-SUP-03 sections admit. The deep readings, readiness index, modeling schema, supplemental reconciliation ledger and audit it links are not curated evidence on this subject and nothing is borrowed from them. The model's strong readiness label and its retrospective holdout probe are inputs, not conclusions. No original manga page, anime adaptation, V1 material or other character's model is included, and the evaluator performed no primary-source inspection.
assessment_scope.temporal_boundary: Chisaki / Overhaul from the V14 League meeting (V14:p124-140) through V15-V17 Hassaikai command, the Eri project and the raid (V15:p009-141, V16:p092-167, V17:p072-170), V18 defeat with loss of both arms and the project (V18:p013-059), V32 disabled captivity fixated on the boss (V32:p107, p149-176) and the V42 meeting with the surviving boss (V42:p082-083), kept as separable snapshots (young Hassaikai planner, raid combatant, disabled captive, postwar listener). Supplement claims on hospital payment, treatment and Quirk modification, and reimprisonment are earlier-only, unresolved or endpoint claims, not enacted scenes. No atom covers V19-V31 or V33-V41.
assessment_scope.assessment_method: characters/RECONSTRUCTION_CAPABILITY_SPEC.md and governance/policies/CHARACTER_RECONSTRUCTION_MAINTENANCE.md at basis_commit; evidence-located calibration with countercases, explicit gaps and no model-readiness inheritance.

dimensions.note: The model states a priority hierarchy (restore the Hassaikai and repay the boss above the autonomy of people made useful to that plan), a feared condition of impotence, an ideal self of managerial efficacy and restored order with selective contamination aversion it says does not prevent violence, and a precise relational failure: real gratitude that overrides the boss's explicit rejection (CO05). It rests on seven located atoms CO01-CO07 at high confidence. Not B: one compact artifact, the model is dense only in organizational and coercive contexts, and it states ordinary life and noninstrumental relationships are missing. Not D: the policy is operational and yields located conditional predictions.

Four snapshots are located and kept apart: young planner (CO01-CO03), raid combatant (CO04-CO05), disabled captive whose policy narrows to reaching the boss (CO06) and postwar listener who cries and apologizes (CO07); the model states defeat changes more than resources and that tears are new state evidence without completed reform. Not B: the post-defeat states rest on two atoms, V19-V31 and V33-V41 are unsampled, and long-term change is stated unknown. Not D: change is located across the series with explicit state selection rules.

Attested features are 俺, clipped directives and plan and hierarchy vocabulary in command contexts, socially plausible paternal framing distinct from private threat (CO02), the self-justifying 恩を返したいだけだ (CO05) and later exposed, repetitive boss-directed apology. The model warns that politeness or a low voice is not benevolence and that the apology's recipient must stay attached. These answer bounded canon questions about register only; the discovery row does not enroll SPEECH.

The only ordinary texture is contamination language and bodily aversion, which the model calls a textual feature rather than a clinical basis, and the supplement's claim that he paid the boss's hospital costs by an unknown mechanism (CO-SUP-02). The model states repeated ordinary life is missing and that its policy does not establish conduct in a neutral friendship.

A five-row partner table (boss, Eri, Nemoto and subordinates, the League, Midoriya and Mirio) gives conditional conduct, and the two central relations are located across states: the boss through gratitude overriding rejection (CO05), captive fixation (CO06), hospital payment (CO-SUP-02) and the V42 reproach scene (CO07, the probe's supported recipient boundary); Eri through coercive guilt (CO02, CO04) and later utility-focused response with no demonstrated apology (CO06). Not B: the League, Nemoto and Midoriya and Mirio rows rest on one or two scenes, and noninstrumental relationships are stated missing. Not D: the boss relation is multi-state with a located recipient boundary.

The self-justification line (CO05), boss fixation and apology-seeking (CO06) and V42 tears are located; the feared condition of impotence and the experience of disorder as dirty are analyst inferences from conduct and contamination language. Not C: no extended reflective window of his own is analyzed, and the model states the relational scope of the tears is set only by their named recipient.

Conflict is a stated policy: define a restoration objective, consolidate authority, turn bodies and capabilities into controlled resources, use public cover when useful, enforce when challenged, and escalate through others and tactical recombination under serious threat. It is located in killing Magne and injuring Compress after refusal (CO01), exploiting Mirio's predictable protection of Eri (CO04) and the defeat that removes his action interface (CO05); the model notes his misjudgment that removing Permeation removes the hero. Not B: one arc of engagements, and the post-defeat state makes earlier combat infeasible. Not D: the policy is explicit, located and yields contrasting predictions.

The model states his operating norm, hierarchical instrumentalism, and the self-justification that rationalizes disassembly and coercive experimentation as means to an orderly future, and keeps gratitude from being read as consent. Not C: no deliberation of his over a moral cost is analyzed, his postwar moral change is stated unestablished, and future Eri-directed conduct is OPEN; the discovery row does not enroll ETHICS.
Nothing in the evidence set establishes humor or play by him, or its absence. This gap says nothing about the character.

The project's analytical corpus is complete for V01-V42 and the three admitted supplements, and the seven atoms span V14-V42 with page locators, the V42 decisive pages directly checked and the V31 page convention explicit. No atom covers V19-V31 or V33-V41, the model does not itemize every appearance, and supplement claims are profile, editorial and author claims, one of them unresolved.

Affirmative limits are located: the model REVISEs the affectless villain and power removal as identity erasure, and REJECTs gratitude as consent, crying as completed accountability and victim restoration as repayment owed; his Permeation theory fails against Mirio's trained skill (CO04); the boss rejects his methods and demands lifelong Eri-directed accountability (CO07) with no Eri meeting depicted; Quirk modification is asserted without restored hands or activation (CO-SUP-01). Not B: the limits rest on a few windows in one artifact.

Snapshots are named by volume and page with the V31 convention stated; the model forbids importing earlier capacity into the armless captive state, granting an unseen repaired interface, or using later knowledge of the boss's survival to make earlier fear fake, and requires chronology selection before predicting emotional restraint. In-world dates are not given and V19-V31 and V33-V41 are unsampled.

scenario_readiness.note: The model states that generated dialogue would be an illustrative prediction, never an attributed quotation, and warns against redirecting boss-directed apology toward Eri or reading politeness as benevolence. Lines beyond the attested forms would be fluent invention. This bounds the evidence set, not Chisaki's actual speech.

conditions: Chronology is one named snapshot: V14-V17 Hassaikai planner, V17-V18 raid combatant, V32 disabled captive or V42 postwar listener, never blended; no V19-V31 or V33-V41 behavior is invented.
The situation carries organizational or relational stakes the policy covers: authority, leverage, the Eri project, or access to the boss.
The interlocutor is the boss, Eri, Nemoto or subordinates, the League, Midoriya or Mirio, handled as the partner table gives, with no invented noninstrumental friendship.
Overhaul is available only in pre-defeat snapshots with contact and material; no restored hands, activation or workaround is assumed after defeat.

Output is a behavioral description with high-confidence behavior, plausible alternatives and flip conditions, abstaining on the model's OPEN items (future Eri-directed conduct, long-term rehabilitation, independent ordinary relations); no quoted dialogue is produced as canon and no readiness is inherited from the strong label.

cross_scenario_scope.assumed_chronology: One named snapshot: Hassaikai planner (V14-V17), raid combatant (V17-V18), disabled captive (V32) or postwar listener (V42), stated explicitly.
cross_scenario_scope.interlocutor_relationship: The boss as attachment figure, Eri as coerced resource, Nemoto or subordinates as selectively recognized followers, the League as antagonistic negotiators, or Midoriya and Mirio as opponents read tactically.
setting_constraints: Organizational command, public confrontation under cover, combat, or custody and a permitted meeting
Overhaul requires the pre-defeat activation interface, contact and material
Remorse stays attached to its named recipient; no completed reform or Eri-directed apology is assumed
No neutral friendship, ordinary domestic, romance or unrelated private-life setting

scenario_readiness.note: The model states three conditional predictions (V15 public confrontation by a cautious hero, V17 imminent defeat, postwar meeting with the rejecting boss) and its probe supports preservation of the recipient boundary. The probe is retrospective and nonblind with a partial relationship axis, and the policy is stated to be domain-specific, so readiness is conditional and narrow.

The model states repeated ordinary life and noninstrumental relationships are missing and that its policy does not establish conduct in a neutral friendship without organizational stakes; independent ordinary relations are OPEN.

The evidence gives his instrumental operating norm and self-justification but no analyzed deliberation; the model rejects tears as completed accountability and leaves future Eri-directed conduct and long-term rehabilitation OPEN. Generating moral weighing or reform would exceed the evidence. This bounds the evidence set, not Chisaki's ethics.
Nothing in the evidence set establishes romantic conduct or its absence. This gap says nothing about the character.

conditions: Hassaikai organizational command in the V14-V18 pre-defeat snapshots, the criminal enterprise being his only modeled working domain.
Planning, recruitment, product development and enforcement as CO01-CO04 show; selective recognition can recruit real loyalty while instrumental disposal stays available.
No legitimate business, postwar institutional or rehabilitative work role is generated.
scenario_readiness.note: His best-evidenced domain is directing a restoration plan through hierarchy, scarce products and leverage, located in CO01-CO05 with the followers' distinction between the boss's authority and his methods (CO03).

known_limits.statement: His gratitude to the boss is real but overrides the boss's explicit rejection of his methods; gratitude is not consent, and selective care for one recipient does not generalize to those he instrumentalizes.

V42 tears and apology are directed to the boss, who demands lifelong confrontation with Eri's suffering; no Eri meeting or victim-directed restitution is depicted, so crying is not completed accountability and the remorse must not be redirected to Eri.

Overhaul depends on the activation interface, contact and material; after defeat both arms and the project are lost, and the supplement's asserted treatment and Quirk modification supply no restored hands, activation method or later use.
Accurate local social prediction, such as Mirio protecting Eri, coexists with a wrong wider theory of personhood: removing Permeation does not remove the hero.

Repeated ordinary life, noninstrumental relationships and demonstrated Eri-directed restitution are missing; future Eri-directed conduct, long-term rehabilitation and independent ordinary relations are OPEN.

Supplement profile facts and editorial summaries (CO-SUP-01 to CO-SUP-03) constrain reconstruction without becoming enacted manga observations; the hospital-payment mechanism is unknown and the Quirk-modification claim is unresolved.

The single formal probe CO-V01 is a retrospective chronological evidence holdout by an analyst who had read later manga, not a blind experiment; its action support is narrow and its relationship-handling axis only partial.
No evidence atom covers V19-V31 or V33-V41, so his conduct in custody over those intervals is not established by this evidence set.

The deep readings, readiness index, supplemental reconciliation ledger and audit linked from the model are not curated evidence on this subject, so their warrants were not independently rechecked here. Anime performance and any supplement material beyond what the model cites lie outside this evidence set. Missing support is not evidence of absence.
